title: Audit Export (SIEM-ready) — Observability Plan (metrics/logs/traces) [DRAFT]
content:
Context
- Project: SIEM-ready audit export (beta). Control-plane service manages export destinations; worker subsystem delivers to sinks (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3).
- This doc is the observability plan for the exporter pipeline (not the underlying audit logging pipeline that produces events).
- Audience: SRE/Observability + Platform teams implementing metrics, logs, traces; Console team consuming health fields.

Goals
1) Make it obvious when a destination is healthy vs degraded vs failing.
2) Provide enough signals to answer:
   - Are we delivering? (success rate)
   - How long does it take? (end-to-end latency)
   - Are we falling behind? (backlog depth / age)
   - Are retries storming / are we throttled? (retry rate, 4xx/5xx classification)
   - Are events landing in DLQ? (DLQ volume + reasons)
3) Provide per-deployment posture (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). In Private, we may not page Redwood on every customer issue, but we still need dashboards + guidance.
4) Create a baseline dashboard + alert set for beta readiness.

Non-goals (beta)
- Full customer-facing cost analytics by destination.
- End-to-end traceability for every event (sampling will be required at higher volumes).
- Building an in-product query builder for customers (console will show health + last error + basic counters only).

Definitions / key concepts
- Destination: configured sink instance (type=splunk|datadog|s3) per tenant/workspace.
- Event: an audit event matching schema v1.
- Attempt: one delivery attempt for an event or batch to a destination.
- Delivered: sink connector returned success semantics (HEC 200 + optional ACK confirmation; Datadog 2xx; S3 put success).
- DLQ: dead-letter queue for events that exceeded retry budget or are deemed non-retriable.

Instrumentation principles
- Labels/tags should be low-cardinality. Avoid tagging by tenant_id directly on high-volume metrics.
  - Recommended: tenant_tier (free|pro|enterprise), deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private), sink_type (splunk|datadog|s3), region, env (prod|staging).
  - For per-tenant debugging, use logs (structured) and on-demand queryable events, or a separate low-QPS metric stream with explicit allowlist.
- Always include:
  - destination_id (ONLY in logs; in metrics this is optional and should be feature-flagged / sampled to avoid cardinality explosions)
  - request_id / trace_id for correlation
  - export_config_version (or updated_at) in logs to debug “config changed and then broke”
- Error classification: standardize across connectors
  - error_class: auth|permission|throttle|timeout|network|sink_5xx|schema|payload_too_large|misconfig|unknown
  - retriable: true|false

Metrics (proposed)
Naming notes
- Assuming Prometheus-style counters/histograms (or OTel -> Prom): snake_case, unit suffixes, *_total for counters.
- If we ship to Datadog metrics directly, preserve tags/units.

A) Throughput + outcomes
1) audit_export_events_enqueued_total
- Count of audit events accepted into export pipeline (post-filtering decision TBD; see note below)
- Labels: deployment_mode, env, region
- Note: consider separate metrics pre-filter and post-filter.

2) audit_export_events_filtered_total
- Count of events dropped due to filtering rules (include/exclude)
- Labels: sink_type (optional), deployment_mode, env
- Include label filter_reason: excluded_by_rule|not_included|invalid_rule|field_not_allowed

3) audit_export_deliveries_attempted_total
- Count of delivery attempts (batch or per-event depending on connector implementation)
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region

4) audit_export_deliveries_succeeded_total
- Count of successful deliveries (same unit as attempted_total)
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region

5) audit_export_deliveries_failed_total
- Count of failed deliveries
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region, error_class, http_status_family (2xx|4xx|5xx|none)

6) audit_export_retry_scheduled_total
- Count of retries scheduled
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, error_class

B) Latency (delivery and backlog)
7) audit_export_delivery_latency_seconds (histogram)
- End-to-end time from “event created_at (or ingested_at) into export queue” -> “delivered_at for that destination”
- Buckets: 1s, 5s, 15s, 30s, 60s, 2m, 5m, 10m, 30m, 60m
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region
- Important: define start timestamp precisely.
  - Proposed start: when exporter worker reads the event from durable queue (queue_dequeued_at)
  - Alternate: when audit log service emits event to export stream. This requires cross-service propagation.
  - For beta we likely track both:
    - worker_delivery_latency (dequeue->delivered)
    - end_to_end_delivery_latency (event_time->delivered) where available

8) audit_export_backlog_depth (gauge)
- Number of events pending across all destinations in queue (or per-destination partitions if we have them)
- Labels: deployment_mode, env, region

9) audit_export_backlog_age_seconds (gauge)
- Age of oldest undelivered event in the queue/partition
- Labels: sink_type (if partitioned by sink_type), deployment_mode, env, region

C) DLQ
10) audit_export_dlq_events_total
- Count of events written to DLQ
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, error_class, dlq_reason (retry_exhausted|non_retriable|schema_violation|poison_pill)

11) audit_export_dlq_depth (gauge)
- Current DLQ size (events)
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region

12) audit_export_dlq_oldest_age_seconds (gauge)
- Age of oldest DLQ event (time since first failure or since DLQ insert)
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region

D) Connector request metrics (per sink)
13) audit_export_connector_request_duration_seconds (histogram)
- Duration of connector HTTP request / S3 put
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region, outcome (success|failure)

14) audit_export_connector_payload_bytes (histogram)
- Payload size per request (batch)
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env

15) audit_export_connector_batch_size (histogram)
- Number of events per batch
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env

16) audit_export_splunk_hec_ack_latency_seconds (histogram)
- Only if ACK enabled; time between submit and ACK confirmation
- Labels: deployment_mode, env, region

E) Rate limiting / backpressure (to protect primary API)
17) audit_export_worker_concurrency (gauge)
- Current worker concurrency
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region

18) audit_export_worker_paused_total (counter)
- Destination pause events triggered automatically or manually
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, pause_reason (operator|circuit_breaker|config_invalid|excessive_errors|customer_request)

19) audit_export_circuit_breaker_open (gauge)
- 0/1 indicator when breaker open per sink_type (or per destination if we can do without cardinality issues)
- Labels: sink_type, deployment_mode, env, region

Notes/questions on metric semantics (open)
- Counters “attempted/succeeded/failed” should align to the same unit:
  - If connectors use batches, we should report both batch outcomes AND event outcomes.
  - Proposed: have *_batches_* metrics AND *_events_* metrics to avoid confusion.
- If we can only do one in beta: prioritize event-level outcomes for success rate and a separate batch size histogram to understand batching.

Structured logs
Where
- audit-export worker service (delivery subsystem)
- audit-export control plane (config changes, state transitions)

Log format (JSON)
Required fields
- timestamp
- service: audit-export-worker | audit-export-control-plane
- env, region, deployment_mode
- sink_type
- destination_id (OK in logs)
- tenant_id (OK in logs; ensure access controls)
- workspace_id (if distinct)
- event_id (audit schema event_id)
- export_attempt_id (generated per attempt)
- batch_id (if applicable)
- trace_id / span_id
- outcome: success|failure|retry_scheduled|dlq
- error_class, error_message (sanitized), http_status, sink_response_code (if any)
- retry_count, next_retry_at
- delivered_at

Log examples (pseudo)
- “delivery_attempt”: includes endpoint host (NOT full URL with secrets), payload_bytes, batch_size
- “delivery_failure”: includes error_class + sanitized response body; add “action_hint” for common errors (e.g., ‘check HEC token permissions’, ‘Datadog API key invalid’, ‘S3 AccessDenied’)
- “destination_state_change”: enabled->degraded->paused

PII / secrets
- DO NOT log auth tokens, API keys, full headers.
- For endpoints, log hostname + path template only (e.g., https://http-inputs-<region>.splunkcloud.com/services/collector)
- Redact any user-provided filter strings if they can include sensitive tokens (not expected, but be safe).

Distributed tracing
- Use OpenTelemetry.
- Tracing spans:
  - dequeue_event
  - apply_filter_rules
  - build_batch
  - connector_send (child span)
  - connector_ack_wait (splunk only)
  - checkpoint_commit
  - dlq_write
- Propagation
  - If upstream audit log system can attach trace_id, propagate; otherwise generate trace at worker dequeue and include event_id + request_id as attributes.
- Sampling
  - Default: 1% traces for success, 100% for failures that are retriable? (cap to prevent storms)
  - Consider dynamic sampling when error rate spikes.

Dashboards (suggested)
1) Overview: Audit Export Health (global)
- Success rate (events) by sink_type (stacked)
- Delivery latency p50/p95/p99 by sink_type
- Backlog depth + backlog age
- DLQ depth + DLQ inserts/min
- Top error_class over last 1h/24h
- Circuit breaker open count / paused destinations

2) Sink-specific dashboards
- Splunk HEC
  - HEC request duration, 4xx vs 5xx
  - ACK latency (if enabled)
  - Common error classes: auth/throttle/sink_5xx
- Datadog
  - Intake endpoint distribution, 429 rate, retry scheduling
- S3
  - PutObject duration, AccessDenied rate, payload_bytes, object write frequency

3) Destination debugging (internal only)
- Destination timeline: last_success_at, last_error_at, recent error classes
- Retry rate and next_retry_at distribution
- Drilldown via logs by destination_id (not a dashboard with high-cardinality metrics)

4) Private deployment dashboard pack
- Same charts but designed to run in customer cluster (Prometheus/Grafana) + minimal alerting guidance.
- Provide a “what to send Redwood Support” panel: exporter version, config version timestamps, last 50 error summaries.

Alerts (beta baseline)
Paging (Hosted/Dedicated)
- High-level: delivery success rate drop
  - Condition: audit_export_deliveries_succeeded_total / attempted_total < 99.5% for 15m (by sink_type) AND attempted_total > threshold
- Backlog age breach
  - Condition: backlog_age_seconds > 10m for 10m (Hosted) (tune per SLO)
- DLQ growth
  - Condition: dlq_events_total rate > N/min for 10m OR dlq_depth increasing for 30m
- Connector auth failures
  - Condition: auth error_class spikes (likely customer action but needs rapid surfacing); route to non-page or page depending on volume

Ticket / non-paging
- Elevated throttle errors (429) over 30m (action: tune backoff / batch sizes; advise customer)
- Increased payload_too_large errors (action: reduce batch sizes)
- Increased schema errors (action: bug/regression; page during rollout window)

SLO alignment (ties to Confluence SLO doc)
- Primary SLI candidates:
  - Delivery latency: p95 end-to-end within target window (TBD per sink)
  - Delivery success rate: delivered events / attempted events (excluding customer misconfig? tbd)
- We need an explicit policy for whether customer misconfiguration counts against SLO (my vote: exclude from platform SLO but still alert; keep separate “customer-caused failure” burn).

Implementation checklist (who/when)
- Metrics
  - [Platform/worker] Add counters/histograms/gauges per above; ensure consistent labels across connectors.
  - [Observability] Define dashboards (Grafana/Datadog) and add to observability-pack.
- Logs
  - [Worker] Ensure structured logs with error_class taxonomy.
  - [Control plane] Log destination state changes + config edits (no secrets).
- Tracing
  - [Worker] Add OTel spans; ensure trace_id injected into logs.
- Rollout
  - Add dashboards first in staging; validate with soak tests (Leila’s matrix)
  - Tune alert thresholds after staging load + beta customer onboarding

Open questions
1) Do we maintain separate queues per destination (enables per-destination backlog metrics) or shared queue + checkpoint (harder to attribute backlog)?
2) For Datadog: do we treat 202 vs 200 differently? (Datadog intake semantics vary.)
3) For Splunk ACK: default on/off for beta? If off, we still need a clear message that 200 != indexed.
4) What’s the canonical timestamp for “event created”? Audit schema has event_time; confirm it’s always present and reliable.
5) Private deployments: which metrics stack is guaranteed (Prometheus?) vs optional.

Appendix: proposed error_class mapping (first pass)
- auth: 401/403 from Splunk/Datadog; S3 AccessDenied
- throttle: 429, explicit Splunk throttling, Datadog rate limit
- sink_5xx: 5xx responses
- timeout: request timeout, context deadline exceeded
- network: DNS/TLS connect errors
- payload_too_large: 413 or connector-side size guardrail
- schema: event fails schema validation / connector payload schema mismatch
- misconfig: invalid endpoint URL, invalid region endpoint selection, missing required config

Changelog
- 2025-02-06: initial draft (AG)
- 2025-02-12: add DLQ metrics + error classification notes (AG, RM)
- 2025-02-18: add tracing spans + private pack section (AB, SG)
